Pen-stroke overlays

Strokes traced by an AI model, not yet reviewed by a human. Claude, an AI model, placed every stroke's median on this page by eye, had a script smooth it into curves, and judged every residual piece, so read the strokes as a draft. Where a stroke is swept by its crop's nib, a script then moved its median to fit the ink, and the nib gives its widths and ends; elsewhere the script fitted its widths and ends to the ink.

Each crop of the Leningrad Codex is drawn four times its size, or twice for a whole line, with its stroke-SVG over it. The checkboxes beside each image switch that image's layers. The profile, and what each layer means, are in doc/pen-stroke-representation.md; this page is generated by py/main_pen_stroke.py render.

Hatched orange, outlined with dashes: a supplied stroke. The crop shows little or no ink of it; it is there because the transcription or the layout implies it. No other stroke is ever drawn this way, and a supplied stroke is never drawn in a stroke's colour or in black.

Slate grey: ink of another word or line, which the crop holds but is not its subject. Its own checkbox hides it.
